Eligible participants are those who are enrolled in PPMI, meet criteria for NSD Stage 2B, are at least 60 years of age, do not have a clinical diagnosis of Parkinson's disease, dementia with Lewy bodies or another neurodegenerative disease, and are not on dopaminergic therapy or a cholinesterase inhibitor.

power.title: Power Analysis Check

table.text: To assess the potential dependence of the results of the primary analysis on missing values, we will conduct a series of sensitivity analyses including comparison of RSSP treatment group to randomized placebo controls (excluding concurrent non-randomized controls), supplemented intention to treat analysis using PPMI data, and various multiple imputation methods. For a regimen, "power" is defined as the probability of demonstrating success on at least one of the primary endpoints. Regimens that enter the platform trial later are expected to see increased power relative to the first regimen due to the accumulation of shared, randomized placebo controls. In addition, the number of non-randomized controls from PPMI that will be available for each regimen analysis are unknown, and a range from 0 to 100 non-randomized control participants were considered in clinical trial simulation. Simulation results estimate power for the first three regimens between 73%-84% to detect treatment effects when both endpoints achieve 40% slowing of progression. Similarly, simulation results demonstrate 67%-77% power to declare success if there is truly a 40% or greater reduction in slope/progression of MDS-UPDRS Part III if there is at least a simultaneous 30% or greater reduction in mean putamen SBR. Finally, we have around 66%-79% probability of declaring success if there is truly a 40% or greater reduction in slope/progression on the DAT SPECT imaging endpoint and at least a 30% reduction on slope/progression on the MDS-UPDRS Part III endpoint. The simulations also demonstrated that the overall type I error probability (probability of meeting the criteria for success when there is no true reduction on either endpoint) was well controlled at 18%. Further details of Bayesian modeling for this study can be found in the companion paper.

text.text: The development of biologically targeted therapeutics (BTTs) that slow Parkinson's disease progression has been hampered by a reliance on testing interventions in clinically defined populations with already advanced pathobiology.

Publications on the biological definition and classification of neuronal -synuclein disease (NSD), and the development of the NSD integrated staging system (NSD-ISS), have generated a framework for identifying individuals with NSD prior to the emergence of a clinically defined syndrome.
Path to Prevention (P2P) is a phase 2A, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled platform trial designed to assess the safety and efficacy of interventions in an early-stage NSD population.

The trial is embedded within the observational Parkinson's Precision Medicine Initiative (PPMI), a structure that enables recruitment of participants from the PPMI cohort, leverages existing operational infrastructure, and utilizes data from non-P2P enrolled PPMI participants in the Bayesian statistical modeling.

P2P will enroll participants at least 60 years of age with NSD Stage 2B (abnormal -synuclein, dopaminergic dysfunction, and prodromal signs or symptoms without functional impairment) without a NOTE: This preprint reports new research that has not been certified by peer review and should not be used to guide clinical practice. clinically defined diagnosis of PD or a related disorder.
As a platform trial, P2P will enable the testing of multiple interventions under a Master Protocol at approximately 35 sites across North America and Europe.
Interventions are selected from industry-submitted applications based on biological relevance of the targets, and on the adequacy of the safety data appropriate to the target population.
Each treatment regimen will have 125 participants on active treatment and at least 125 shared placebo control participants.
Participants will remain on treatment for a maximum of 144 weeks or until 96 weeks since the randomization of the last participant.

P2P has two primary endpoints, 1) rate of change in mean putamen specific binding ratio from baseline through follow-up and, 2) rate of change in the MDS-UPDRS Part III motor examination from baseline through follow-up or initiation of dopaminergic treatment.
A range of secondary and exploratory biomarker-focused endpoints will be assessed.
The protocol was developed with input from multiple stakeholders, including people with early-stage NSD, biopharmaceutical industry leaders, and regulatory authorities.

P2P is the first trial to test biologically targeted assets in biologically defined prodromal participants utilizing an efficient platform design, which will provide the field with tools to expand therapeutic development, and enable intervention at earlier stages of neurodegeneration.
P2P is scheduled to begin enrollment in December 2026 and is committed to data sharing and broad dissemination of learnings from the study.
The single largest unmet need in Parkinson's disease and related disorders is for biologically targeted therapeutics (BTTs) that slow and ultimately prevent disease progression.
In the absence of a biological definition for Parkinson's disease, potential BTTs have historically been tested in clinically defined populations.

However, by the time a clinical diagnosis of Parkinson's disease can be established, the underlying pathobiology is already fairly advanced, [1] [2] [3] and may be too advanced for successful disease modification.

text.text: Intervening before the onset of a clinically defined syndrome may be a more successful strategy for slowing disease progression and preventing disability.

While Parkinson's disease has characteristic prodromal features (including hyposmia, REM sleep behavior disorder, dysautonomia, and mood impairment) that enable the identification of individuals before a clinical diagnosis, the lack of understanding of the natural history of the earliest (prediagnosis) stages of disease and the absence of a clear regulatory-acceptable definition for prodromal Parkinson's disease has prohibited the conduct of clinical trials of BTTs in this population.
However, with recent advancements, we are now prepared to initiate such trials.

The development of reliable biomarkers for α-synuclein pathology has led to the emergence of biological disease frameworks, including the neuronal α-synuclein disease integrated staging system (NSD-ISS) and SynNeurGe, that define disease based on the presence of α-synuclein pathology. 4, 5 These frameworks have enabled the identification of individuals much earlier in the disease course, prior to the emergence of the clinically defined syndromes of Parkinson's disease and dementia with Lewy bodies, and empowered therapeutic development.

text.text: P2P will be embedded within PPMI, thereby enabling the use of existing study infrastructure and recruitment of participants directly from PPMI.
P2P will use an innovative platform design that will enable the testing of multiple BTTs under a master protocol with efficient use of shared placebo controls and unifying study infrastructure.

As the first interventional clinical trial in the field to examine the potential for BTTs to slow progression in a biologically defined prodromal Parkinson's disease population, P2P is also a learning study intended to inform the broader field and advance the development of BTTs in this population.

Key anticipated learnings relate to the paradigm for participant selection and recruitment, measurement of disease progression in the context of an early interventional study, endpoint performance in a population pre-clinical diagnosis, and advancement of regulatory science.
Here, we describe the design of P2P and discuss key trial design considerations.
The companion manuscript by Wendelberger et al describes the modeling that informed the design of the trial and statistical considerations.

P2P is a multi-center, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled platform trial designed to evaluate the safety and efficacy of multiple investigational products for the treatment of early-stage NSD (Figure 1).

text.text: A Master Protocol provides the overall framework for the trial and enables the testing of multiple investigational products both simultaneously and sequentially.

A regimen consists of an investigational product and matched placebo control and each regimen is described in a Regimen Specific Sub-Protocol (RSSP) that dictates procedures, assessments, and testing unique to that investigational product.

In a two-step randomization process, participants are randomized first in an equal manner to one of K actively enrolling regimens and then in a K:1 manner to active treatment or placebo control within the regimen.
The first step (regimen assignment) is unblinded and the second step (treatment assignment) is blinded.

Each regimen will have approximately 125 participants on active treatment and approximately 125 shared placebo control participants; the number of shared placebo controls will depend on the number of prior and actively enrolling regimens.
Participants will remain on treatment for a maximum of 144 weeks or until 96 weeks since the randomization of the last participant.
The Master Protocol is provided in the Supplementary Materials.
Platform trials like P2P have many operational efficiencies.
With traditional clinical trial designs, the number of treatment arms and the trial duration are prespecified and usually limited.
Moreover, trial infrastructure must be assembled prior to study initiation and then disassembled at the conclusion.

In contrast, platform trials can test multiple investigational products over time (either simultaneously or sequentially) under the same master protocol using the same trial infrastructure and have no defined end date, enabling investigational products to be added as they become available.

The use of the same sites, investigators, coordinators, and procedures provides both cost and time advantages that may support faster and more efficient decision-making regarding whether or not to move therapeutic research forward. 18 Platform trials also enable uniform clinical, biological, and neuroimaging data acquisition across the testing of multiple investigational products, which minimizes the need to train staff on new procedures each time a new regimen is added.

text.text: Beyond operational efficiencies, platform trials have certain statistical efficiencies, as they enable sharing of placebo controls across different treatment arms and enable learnings about endpoint behavior to be incorporated into future iterations of the Master Protocol, which is important given the novel study population.

Placebo effects are a well-recognized challenge in Parkinson's disease clinical trials 23 and require special consideration in platform trials, where multiple agents are tested against a shared placebo control group.

text.text: P2P will consider testing agents with oral, intramuscular, and intravenous routes of administration, but not more invasive routes of administration (e.g., intrathecal, neurosurgical) given safety and feasibility considerations.
In P2P, each regimen will include a placebo control that is matched to the investigational product associated with that RSSP based on formulation, route of administration, and dosing regimen.
P2P will have multiple types of controls.
For analysis of a given treatment regimen, placebo data across regimens will be shared to produce a single placebo control dataset for analyses.
The sharing of placebo between regimens has clear statistical advantages and enables modeling of differential responses to placebo (e.g., intravenous versus oral).
As a perpetual platform trial, there may be substantial time gaps between enrollment in the first arm and enrollment in the last arm.

The use of Bayesian modeling with hierarchical borrowing allows for heterogeneity across individual baseline values and individual slopes, as well as heterogeneity across regimens due to minor differences in the inclusion/exclusion criteria or mode of administration and will partially mitigate the impact of temporal and placebo differences.
See Wendelberger et al for more on the use of dynamic borrowing.
PPMI has a robust infrastructure, which is critical to the success of P2P.

text.text: Three, enrollment based on NSD Stage 2B status provides a clear and reproducible definition to replace the prior poorly defined term of prodromal disease.

Lastly and essentially important, NSD Stage 2B demonstrates progression within a typical clinical trial timeframe; 21% of stage 2B PPMI participants without a clinical diagnosis progressed to functional impairment at year 1, 34% at year 2, and 43% at year 3. 33 While earlier stage NSD populations (Stages 1-2A, individuals with a positive α-synuclein biomarker but no evidence of dopaminergic deficit and/or nor clinical symptoms or signs) may be reasonable for inclusion in future trials, at the present time, sufficient longitudinal data does not exist to inform understanding of progression and enrichment in these earlier stage populations. 34 Lastly, later stages (Stages 3-6) are defined by the presence of functional impairment and the majority of participants in these stages are expected to have a clinically defined diagnosis. 4 However, even among NSD Stage 2B there is heterogeneity of the clinical phenotype (see below).

text.text: The clinical cohort includes more than 2800 classically defined prodromal participants with hyposmia, with RBD, and genetically at-risk for PD.
As of July 2026, there are 2593 active prodromal participants in PPMI, of whom 1748 have NSD.

Of these, 476 are NSD stage 2B; this includes participants with polysomnography-confirmed REM sleep behavior disorder (14%, n = 65), hyposmia (40%, n = 191), and hyposmia plus dream enactment behavior (43%, n = 207).

Furthermore, 437 are at least 60 years of age, do not have a clinical diagnosis of Parkinson's disease, dementia with Lewy bodies, or another neurodegenerative disease, and are not taking a dopaminergic medication.
Outreach and screening will continue to meet P2P enrollment needs.
While we cannot accurately predict the proportion of these potentially eligible participants who will enroll in P2P, PPMI has set the foundation providing encouraging indicators.

text.text: P2P is thus well-positioned to successfully screen and enroll participants based on NSD status and to test biologically targeted interventions in this population.
P2P is the first interventional trial to enroll participants based on NSD status.
As a result, no regulatory precedent exists to inform the selection of endpoints.
Outcome measures developed to assess clinical benefit in Parkinson's disease may or may not be appropriate for use in an at-risk population.

The U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) defines meaningful clinical benefit as the effect an intervention has on how someone feels, functions, or survives. 42 However, individuals with early-stage NSD may have minimal symptoms, and by definition, do not have functional impairment.

text.text: This creates difficulties in the selection of an appropriate clinical endpoint.
Thus, one of the goals of P2P is to generate the evidence needed to establish endpoints for this population.

We have done extensive modeling based on PPMI longitudinal data and arrived at the concept of using multiple primary endpoints which means that if a regimen is positive on one, it is considered a positive result.

P2P will test whether treatment slows the rate of progression in a biomarker endpoint, DAT SPECT mean putamen SBR from baseline through follow-up, and a clinical endpoint, MDS-UPDRS Part III 43 score from baseline through follow-up or initiation of dopaminergic treatment.

As an example, time to phenoconversion to clinically manifest Parkinson's disease or dementia with Lewy bodies will be included as an exploratory endpoint.
While this endpoint has face validity as a clinical endpoint, it is inherently subjective.

Moreover, annual phenoconversion rates are low; in an analysis of PPMI participants with RBD who were NSD Stage 2B or higher, only 33% phenoconverted over four years of follow up. 30 Similarly, in an analysis of NSD Stage 2B PPMI prodromal participants, an estimated 4% phenoconverted at year one, 10% at year two, and 18% at year 3. 33 Use of time to phenoconversion as a primary endpoint would therefore require prolonged trial follow-up.

text.text: An essential part of P2P is extensive biomarker characterization of the participants.
Whole blood, urine, CSF, and skin biopsies will be collected for biomarker analysis using PPMI protocols, which will bolster biological understanding of the study population.
For example, integration of biomarkers of neurodegeneration (e.g., amyloid, tau) will inform understanding of the influence of multi-pathology on treatment response.
Similarly, biomarkers of different mechanistic pathways (e.g., neuroinflammation) will inform understanding of the influence of different etiological mechanisms on treatment response.
The complete list of endpoints, including other exploratory endpoints, are included in the Supplementary Materials.

In trials for the earliest stages of Alzheimer's disease, the FDA has demonstrated willingness, to consider changes on neuropsychological testing based on the size, breadth, and statistical robustness of the effect, as sufficient to establish meaningful clinical benefit when supported by biomarker evidence of effect. 48 The European Medicines Agency is developing new guidelines to inform the development of treatments for Alzheimer's disease that will consider appropriate endpoint selection in the early stages of Alzheimer's disease and trial design in biologically defined pre-clinical Alzheimer's disease. 43 However, it is unclear how best to translate this to early-stage NSD, where individuals may meet criteria for Stage 2B based on motor symptoms, cognitive symptoms, or other non-motor symptoms (e.g., RBD, hyposmia) and exhibit different trajectories to different clinically defined syndromes.

text.text: There is no established regulatory pathway for studies testing therapeutics in prodromal synucleinopathies in part due to the lack of an operational definition for prodromal disease.
Biologically defining prodromal disease based on NSD status fills this critical gap.

In early stages of preparation for the study launch, the team engaged with the US and European regulatory authorities to initiate the dialogue on the acceptance of the definition of the population, platform study design, selection of the endpoints and other aspects of the study design.

Both regulatory authorities provided valuable input in the context of Type C meetings in US and Trial Innovation Consultation with EMA, followed by country-specific Scientific Advise in the Netherlands and Germany.
We received constructive feedback that was incorporated into the protocol.
The regulatory authorities specifically highlighted the importance of biologically defining and staging the target population using the NSD-ISS framework in these early-stage development studies.
The FDA Investigational New Drug (IND) application was filed using the NSD definition of the population and was granted "you may proceed status."
An EMA package will be submitted.

The Bayesian primary analysis models estimate a difference in the rate of change of each primary endpoint from baseline through last visit (or, for the MDS-UPDRS Part III, through initiation of dopaminergic treatment).
Each primary endpoint will be tested with equal priority with respect to active treatment superiority versus shared placebo controls.
For both primary endpoints, a Bayesian repeated measures model of outcome will be used to compare the slope of active treatment versus a shared group of placebo and non-randomized controls.

The model allows for heterogeneity across individual baseline values and individual slopes, as well as heterogeneity across regimens due to minor differences in the eligibility criteria or mode of administration.

For each endpoint, if the Bayesian posterior probability of active treatment superiority (H a ) is greater than or equal to a prespecified threshold of 0.90, the null hypothesis (H 0 ) will be rejected, and the active treatment will be deemed superior to placebo control (i.e., less progression on active treatment) with respect to mean endpoint.

This decision threshold of 0.90 has been calibrated via simulation to control the regimen-specific one-sided type I error at approximately 10% per endpoint per regimen (or 20% joint when considering both primary endpoints).

It is hypothesized that an effective treatment will (1)   decrease the progression rate and slow the decline in mean putamen SBR and/or, (2) decrease the progression rate and slow the increase in clinical symptoms as measured by the MDS-UPDRS Part III score.

The primary analyses for each analysis regimen will be based on the intent-to-treat (ITT) principle and include all participants randomized to the active treatment arm of the analysis regimen and all shared controls, regardless of the adherence to the assigned RSSP or duration of follow-up.

Sensitivity analyses will be conducted using an ITT population that consists of participants randomized to the active treatment arm of the analysis regimen and (1) all shared P2P placebo controls (RSSP placebo, concurrent placebo, and non-concurrent placebo controls), (2) P2P concurrent controls (RSSP placebo, concurrent placebo), and (3) RSSP placebo controls.
Lastly, we will also replicate the primary analyses using a per-protocol population.
No interim efficacy or futility analyses are planned.

Analyses to examine safety of each active treatment versus RSSP placebo controls will involve comparisons of the percentage of participants within each RSSP reporting treatment emergent AEs, treatment emergent SAEs, and unanticipated SAEs within each MedDRA (Medical Dictionary for Regulatory Activities) system organ class and preferred terms.

To examine tolerability, within each RSSP we will compare the percentage of participants on treatment vs regimen-specific placebo control group who complete the full RSSP on their initially assigned treatment regimen, regardless of reason for non-completion.
Key feasibility metrics include enrollment timelines, retention, and visit compliance.
Secondary analyses will include an ITT population consisting of all participants randomized to the active treatment arm or shared placebo control arm within an RSSP.
Handling of key exploratory endpoints are as detailed in the Supplementary Material.

To assess the potential dependence of the results of the primary analysis on missing values, we will conduct a series of sensitivity analyses including comparison of RSSP treatment group to randomized placebo controls (excluding concurrent non-randomized controls), supplemented intention to treat analysis using PPMI data, and various multiple imputation methods.
For a regimen, "power" is defined as the probability of demonstrating success on at least one of the primary endpoints.
Regimens that enter the platform trial later are expected to see increased power relative to the first regimen due to the accumulation of shared, randomized placebo controls.

In addition, the number of non-randomized controls from PPMI that will be available for each regimen analysis are unknown, and a range from 0 to 100 non-randomized control participants were considered in clinical trial simulation.
Simulation results estimate power for the first three regimens between 73%-84% to detect treatment effects when both endpoints achieve 40% slowing of progression.

Similarly, simulation results demonstrate 67%-77% power to declare success if there is truly a 40% or greater reduction in slope/progression of MDS-UPDRS Part III if there is at least a simultaneous 30% or greater reduction in mean putamen SBR.

Finally, we have around 66%-79% probability of declaring success if there is truly a 40% or greater reduction in slope/progression on the DAT SPECT imaging endpoint and at least a 30% reduction on slope/progression on the MDS-UPDRS Part III endpoint.

The simulations also demonstrated that the overall type I error probability (probability of meeting the criteria for success when there is no true reduction on either endpoint) was well controlled at 18%.
Further details of Bayesian modeling for this study can be found in the companion paper.

A Therapeutic Evaluation Committee, comprised of international experts in pharmacology, biomarkers, and clinical trials design, is charged with the review and prioritization of potential investigational products for testing.

The selection of interventions for P2P is based on biological relevance to an early-stage NSD population, safety data, appropriateness for testing in a platform trial infrastructure, and partnership readiness (e.g., availability of drug supply and willingness to comply with the P2P governance). 15 As earlystage NSD is defined by the presence of neuronal α-synuclein pathology, α-synuclein provides a compelling target; however, other mechanistic pathways (e.g., inflammation) are also relevant at this stage of disease.

text.text: Testing BTTs in a population without functional impairment that may never develop clinically defined disease, requires careful consideration of safety.
Accordingly, only investigational products that have been tested in humans and have an established, acceptable safety profile will move forward.
The Therapeutics Evaluation Committee also takes operational aspects, such as frequency and route of administration, into consideration.
The final decision regarding the selection of investigational products for testing is made by the P2P Steering Committee.

text.text: P2P, like PPMI, is committed to rapid, accessible data sharing and to the broad and timely distribution of study results.
P2P participants will continue to contribute data to the PPMI data repository in real-time for the assessments and visits that align with the PPMI schedule of activities.
To support data sharing, the schedule of assessments for the annual visits (Baseline, W48, W96, W144) has been constructed to align to the extent possible with the PPMI schedule of assessments.
We have carefully considered potential or perceived risks of unblinding due to data sharing and concluded that these are exceedingly low.
Notably, the shared data will not include any study identifiers.
Moreover, any data specific to the P2P protocol or that carries risk of unblinding will be sequestered in accordance with industry standards until completion and publication of the relevant RSSP.

The most time-consuming aspects of overall study preparation included conceptual design, stakeholders' alignment, iterative statistical modeling adjusted based on an ever-expanding and maturing PPMI cohort dataset and selecting appropriate partnerships with pharma companies.
Active study prelaunch activities started in December 2025.
An updated Master Protocol and the first RSSP were submitted to FDA in April 2026.

Submissions to the relevant regulatory authorities in the United Kingdom, Europe and Canada are anticipated later this year.
The first U.S. participant is expected to be screened in the last quarter of 2026.
We expect that learnings from the P2P planning phase will substantially facilitate and shorten timelines for the launch of future studies testing BTTs in early NSD.
Conclusions Therapeutic interventions that slow neurodegeneration are urgently needed and intervening earlier in the disease process may provide our best chance of success.

P2P is a first-in-field platform trial that will take advantage of new biological frameworks and the success of PPMI to test the safety and early efficacy of the most promising BTTs in early-stage NSD.
P2P includes multiple novel aspects.
Learnings from the study will provide much needed tools for the broader research field and accelerate therapeutic development in populations at earlier stages of neurodegeneration.
